lines.trans: Look at Table Three—everyone on Jasmine Street has merged into one giant blue jellyfish!
Here is a clean towel for your sleeves, boss; at least the water stayed cool.
Honestly, Mazen, abstract watercolour art is very fashionable in cafés right now!
How can twenty-eight neighbours sit down tomorrow without a civilized seating plan?!
Calm down and think—your head still remembers where every single neighbour belongs, right?
Of course I remember every seat, Tariq, but wind blows paper cards off outdoor tables!
He has a point, Tariq; even folded paper place cards flew away ten minutes ago.
Paper flies away only when nobody clips it to something heavy.
Clip it? With what—heavy iron horseshoes on clean white linen napkins?!
Stay right here, drink five sips of mint tea, and let me check my workshop drawer.
First help Rami rescue those tangled lanterns overhead before the cord knots tight, Tariq!
Lanterns first, windproof seats second—nobody panic on my watch.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: At least the bread is ready in the oven.
We need less than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.en: people; family; folks of a place
meanings.note: Collective noun used both for one's family (أهلي 'my family') and the residents of a street or town (أهل الحارة).

examples.trans: All the neighbourhood folks are invited for tea.
My family has lived in Amman for a long time.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Form VII verb used for colours, ink, or groups blending smoothly together.

examples.trans: The colours blended together with the rain.
The guests mingled quickly at the party.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of عقد ('to tie a knot'). Spoken Jordanian uses it for cords getting knotted.

examples.trans: The rope got knotted tight from the wind.
The thread knots up if you pull it fast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Used in ملح بحر ('sea salt') as well as for the Mediterranean or Dead Sea.

examples.text: حطيت رشة صغيرة من ملح البحر فوق العجينة.
examples.trans: I put a tiny pinch of sea salt on top of the dough.

examples.text: هوا البحر بيجي لطيف ومنعش آخر النهار.
examples.trans: The sea breeze comes in gentle and refreshing late in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطاقات.

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Formed from تجريد ('abstraction'). Feminine singular: تجريدية.

examples.trans: Abstract art has bold colours.
This painting is very abstract.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوتر, بيتوتر).

examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences turn long!

examples.text: لا تتوتر، كل شي رح يمشي تمام.
examples.trans: Do not get nervous, everything will go fine.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

ثبّت.gloss: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place

meanings.en: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place
meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'seat securely / hold steady'.

examples.text: طارق ثبت اللوحة النحاس ببراغي صغار.
examples.trans: Tariq fastened the brass plate with small screws.

examples.text: امسك السلم من تحت وثبته منيح.
examples.trans: Hold the ladder at the bottom and steady it well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural حبال (hibaal).

examples.trans: Pull the rope tight on the tree.
We tied the lanterns with a sturdy cord.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Feminine noun sharing its root with حذاء ('shoe'). Plural: حذوات.

examples.trans: An iron horseshoe is very heavy.

examples.text: علقوا حذوة قديمة فوق باب الورشة.
examples.trans: They hung an old horseshoe above the workshop door.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic word for horse. Plural: أحصنة or خيل.

examples.trans: The horse runs fast across the plain.
We drew a small horse on the paper.

meanings.note: Used in معك حق ('you are right / you have a point').

examples.trans: You are right, the weather is cold today.
Everyone has a right to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: روس.

examples.trans: My glasses were on my head!

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من السقف الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رشفات.

examples.trans: Take a sip of cold water first.
He took a small sip of the coffee.

meanings.note: The imperative روق (rawwiq, to a man) or روقي (to a woman) means 'chill, relax'. Related to رايق, calm and in a good mood.

examples.text: روقي يا بنت، لسا في وقت.
examples.trans: Relax, girl, there is still time.
I drink my coffee and relax a bit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشرب, بيشرب).

examples.trans: Drink hot tea first.

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من شوربة الخضار.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the vegetable soup.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Used constantly as بصراحة or bare صراحة ('honestly / to be frank').

examples.trans: Honestly, I loved the place very much.
Frankly, the coffee here is excellent.

meanings.en: huge; massive; large in scale or volume
meanings.note: Feminine ضخمة, plural ضخام. Used for big shapes, large crowds, or oversized objects.

examples.trans: They hung a huge lantern in the middle of the courtyard.

examples.text: موج البحر بالصورة كان ضخم كتير.
examples.trans: The sea wave in the picture was very massive.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.en: to fly; soar; blow away in the wind
meanings.note: Hollow verb (بطير / طار). Used both for birds/aircraft flying and light objects blowing away in a gust.

examples.trans: The sheet of paper flew away with the gust of wind.
The birds flew off from the top of the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Warm, reassuring 'of course! / naturally!'.

examples.trans: Of course, Tariq, your secret is safe with us!
Of course I came when I got your card.

طيّر.gloss: to blow away; make fly; knock off

meanings.en: to make fly; blow away; send flying
meanings.note: Form II causative of طار ('to fly'): الهوا طيّر الورقة ('the wind blew the paper away').

examples.text: هبة الهوا طيّرت الورق عن الطاولة.
examples.trans: The gust of wind blew the papers off the table.

examples.text: الولد عم بيطيّر طيارته الورق عالسطح.
examples.trans: The boy is flying his paper kite on the roof.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفحص, بيفحص).

examples.trans: Tariq will inspect the cellar right away.
We checked the heater and pipes this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.en: art; artistic skill; branch of art
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural فنون) covering painting, craft, and fine arts.

examples.text: بشوف إنه هاد العمل فن حقيقي.
examples.trans: I think this piece is genuine art.

examples.text: مازن بحب كل أنواع الفن والرسم.
examples.trans: Mazen loves all kinds of art and drawing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فوط.

examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water.
She wiped the table with a damp cloth.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقعد, بيقعد).

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.en: hanging oil or candle lamp; small lantern
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural قناديل), traditional Levant term alongside فانوس.

examples.text: ضوّوا قناديل الحوش قبل ما تيجي الناس.
examples.trans: They lit the courtyard lamps before the people arrived.

examples.text: عندي قنديل نحاس قديم من بيت جدي.
examples.trans: I have an old brass oil lamp from my grandfather's house.

meanings.note: Masculine material noun used both for woven linen fabric and flax/linen twine.

examples.text: هاد المريول مصنوع من قماش الكتان البارد.
examples.trans: This apron is made from cool linen fabric.
Linen holds up well in summer and its heat.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing 'sleeve' (kumm, pl. kmaam كمام) from كم ('how many?').

examples.text: شمرت عن كمامي قبل ما نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: I rolled up my sleeves before we washed the windows.

examples.text: تبللت كمام قميصي لما ركضنا تحت المطر.
examples.trans: My shirt sleeves got soaked when we ran in the rain.

meanings.note: Means 'still' in affirmative sentences (لسا سليم 'still intact') and 'not yet' alone or with negation (لسا؟ 'not yet?').

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from ماء ('water'): دهان مائي = 'water-based paint'.

examples.text: الحمد لله الدهان مائي وبيروح بالمي الدافية.
examples.trans: Thankfully the paint is water-based and comes right off with warm water.

examples.text: الدهان المائي ريحته خفيفة وبينشف خلال ساعة.
examples.trans: Water-based paint has a mild smell and dries within an hour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متذكرة, plural: متذكرين).

examples.trans: Do you still remember that story after all these years?
I remember the building number well.

meanings.note: Form VI participle adjective (feminine متشابكة, plural متشابكين) used for tangled strings or interlaced lines.

examples.trans: The strings got tangled up inside the bag.

examples.text: الخطوط المتشابكة عطت شكل حلو للفانوس.
examples.trans: The crisscrossed lines gave the lantern a lovely shape.

meanings.note: Used for architectural/room floor plans, schedules, and blueprints.

examples.text: رسمنا المخطط الجديد للطاولات بملف الاستقبال.
examples.trans: We drew the new table floor plan in the front-desk folder.

examples.text: حسب المخطط في مكان مريح لست طاولات بالساحة.
examples.trans: According to the layout there is comfortable room for six tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرتبة, plural: مرتبين).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Formal/signboard Arabic word for 'café' (alongside conversational كافيه), ideal for painted signs.

examples.text: كتبنا عاللوحة: مقهى جنينة الغرفة تسعة.
examples.trans: We painted on the sign: Room Nine Garden Café.

examples.text: المقهى رح يفتح يوميا من الصبح للمسا.
examples.trans: The café will be open daily from morning till evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناشف.

examples.trans: The room has clean white towels.
Here is a dry towel after the rain.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural موضات) borrowed from European 'moda / mode', also used idiomatically for 'out of fashion' (موضة قديمة).

examples.text: الورق السادة صار موضة قديمة عند الرسامين.
examples.trans: Plain paper has become old-fashioned among painters.
This design is in fashion this year.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Tea with fresh mint warms the heart.
We planted mint in the courtyard beside the tree.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ورشات.

examples.trans: There is a brass lamp in my workshop downstairs.
The old bag is from my grandfather's workshop.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
